headline: High risk: Cursor’s writable, networked workspace can conflict with caveman’s MCP-enabled content workflows, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP server outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content can steer its agent loop. Caveman touches project notes and CLAUDE.md and uses MCP, creating a plausible bridge where content written by one can be parsed as instructions by the other. The shared-file/MCP pathway is documented in both profiles.
conditions: IF caveman writes untrusted text into project notes or CLAUDE.md that Cursor later opens
IF Cursor ingests MCP or clipboard content originating from caveman without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on any file passed between agents
Turn off Cursor Yolo mode for shared folders
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers around MCP/file handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files, but Cursor additionally reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers/MCP servers. Caveman handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. That creates a default pathway for sensitive local content to flow from caveman-managed files into Cursor’s third-party inference path.
conditions: IF caveman stores secrets or sensitive notes in project files
IF Cursor opens those files while connected to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Use separate OS users or workspaces
Disable cloud model providers for the shared project
Review open buffers before invoking Cursor agent mode
requires-engineering: enforce file-level redaction before model upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; caveman supports multiple instances and uses files plus MCP. Because caveman is not runnable itself but is a content-writing workflow that can coexist with Cursor in the same workspace, overlapping writes to shared files and git state can race or overwrite each other without locking. The conflict is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF Cursor auto-runs edits while caveman writes CLAUDE.md or project notes
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on file and MCP inputs, while caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that may be treated as guidance. If Cursor treats caveman output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits, shell actions, or commits. The pathway is plausible from both profiles, but verification is not explicit, so severity stays medium.
conditions: IF caveman-generated notes are fed into Cursor without review
IF Cursor agent mode is allowed to execute follow-on actions from those notes
mitigations: Require human review before Cursor acts on caveman output
Mark caveman notes as untrusted input
Disable auto-run for follow-on commands
Use a checklist for any generated task list
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, but both agents can handle local project content and Cursor may send data to external model providers. Caveman’s docs-only profile does not specify compliance controls, so the main issue is a potential policy gap rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises only when paired with Cursor’s external transmission path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared project files
IF Cursor routes that data to external model providers without an approved DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use a non-regulated test project
Confirm provider/data-processing settings in Cursor
Document retention expectations for shared files
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
